<thought>Using the ESI mass spectrum, the base peak at m/z 276.0666 likely corresponds to [M+H]+. Subtracting the proton mass gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈275.0593 Da. The prominent M+2 peak (~33 % of the base) matches the isotopic pattern of a single chlorine atom (Cl‑35/Cl‑37). Removing the monoisotopic mass of ^35Cl (34.9689 Da) leaves 240.0904 Da to be accounted for by C, H, and O. The combination C₁₂H₁₆O₅ fits this residual mass most closely (calculated neutral mass = 275.0686 Da, only ~9 mDa higher, the best among plausible formulas). Therefore the molecular formula is C₁₂H₁₆O₅Cl. </thought>
<final_answer>C12H16O5Cl</final_answer>
